questions.question: State the three main components of Atkinson and Shiffrin's multi-store model of memory.
Explain how maintenance rehearsal can influence the transfer of information from short-term memory to long-term memory, citing relevant research evidence.
Describe the serial position effect and discuss how it provides evidence for the multi-store model.
Compare the capacity and duration of the sensory register with those of short-term memory.
Evaluate the strengths and weaknesses of the multi-store model in explaining memory errors.
State the main components of Baddeley and Hitch's working memory model.
Explain the role of the central executive in the working memory model and give an example of a task that requires its use.
Describe how the phonological loop and visuospatial sketchpad operate independently and interact within working memory.
Compare episodic buffer with the other components of the working memory model, highlighting its unique functions.
Evaluate the evidence supporting the existence of the episodic buffer as a distinct component of working memory.
Define episodic memory and give an example of a real-life situation where it is used.
Explain the difference between semantic and procedural memory, providing an example for each.
Describe an experiment that demonstrates the distinction between episodic and semantic memory.
Compare the characteristics of episodic, semantic and procedural memory in terms of content, acquisition and retrieval.
Evaluate the role of rehearsal in the consolidation of procedural memory.
